sections.content: How many people are "property, housing and estate managers"?

186,200 people

were counted on the census as "property, housing and estate managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Property, housing and estate managers manage shopping centres, residential areas, offices and private estates, arrange for the sale, purchase, rental and leasing of property on behalf of clients and employers, and provide facilities management services for businesses.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "property, housing and estate managers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "property, housing and estate managers", 14.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "property, housing and estate managers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "property, housing and estate managers" included:

  • managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services
  • education advisers and school inspectors
  • counsellors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "property, housing and estate managers" there were more men than women (58.9% compared with 41.1%).

This means "property, housing and estate managers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 58.9% and women made up 41.1% of "property, housing and estate managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "property, housing and estate managers" included:

  • data analysts
  • managers and proprietors in other services (other)
  • environment professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "property, housing and estate managers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "property, housing and estate managers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "property, housing and estate managers", 9.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (67.7% compared with 32.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (63.5%) than self-employed (36.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Barnet, this is in the same region of London.
